expectationResult: Both missed. S0 miscalibrated against our OWN v10 data (right-despite-wrong-step ~0.55 already said the flat path answers without the steps — should have predicted B-only DIRECT ~0.5). S1 fails because stepping adds nothing over the flat circuit (AB d1 ~= B d1).
gates: PASS 9/9 (A-own 1.0, B-own 1.0, AB-own 0.99-1.0; eval gates all PASS). Fragments are learned; the failure is compositional, not a training failure.
mechanism: Two findings. (1) The tutor DOES acquire both fragments and they coexist in AB weights (both step-rates well above chance) — piecing-together at the SKILL level works. But mixing degrades each (A-training hurts B's flat circuit: AB direct 0.36-0.47 < B direct 0.53-0.61). (2) Explicit stepwise decomposition is REDUNDANT here: B's one-pass forward already bridges both hops (query-sensitivity stays low per v10 diag; every query on the flat returns e-ish, strongest from the doubled token m: oracle 0.79 > direct 0.57). The brain compiles the composition flat instead of showing its work. So: skills piece together in the weights, but the ASSEMBLY happens in one forward pass, not via the DECOMP-1 stepping protocol.
reading: FRAGMENT-FAIL on S0, FAIL on S1 — but the credit-assignment half is a clean PASS-as-designed and it reframes the program: stop testing whether the tutor STEPS through compositions (v10, scale, S1 all say no value-add) and start testing whether the flat forward COMPILES them (B-only direct 0.53-0.61 from pure 1-hop training IS the compiled-composition phenomenon, unclaimed). Proposed (not run): a hard assembly where the flat circuit provably cannot bridge — doubled-token distractors (many doubled keys, only one true chain) or cross-regime hops (step-1 key-valued + step-2 long-regime) — so stepping is REQUIRED, not redundant.
